mainTopic: The end of the story of פנחס and זמרי, and whether a כהן who served while טמא is liable to מיתה בידי שמים
overview: The amud finishes the story of פנחס and זמרי. פנחס tricks שבט שמעון into letting him in, and רבי יוחנן lists six miracles that helped him kill זמרי and כזבי. פנחס then argues with הקב"ה to stop the plague, which רבי אלעזר learns from the word ויפלל. The tribes mock his family background, but the תורה traces his line to אהרן, and הקב"ה has משה greet him with peace. The גמרא then gives more details about the sin and explains the real names of כזבי and זמרי. Next it returns to the משנה's case of a כהן who served while טמא. רב ששת proves from the משנה that he is not liable to מיתה בידי שמים. רב אחא בר הונא pushes back with the rule that people do not kill someone the Torah exempts, and he answers each of רב ששת's four counter-cases. The amud ends as רב אחא בר הונא starts a challenge from a ברייתא about Temple tasks done outside the מקדש, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: פנחס walks up to the tribe of שמעון
steps.stepSummary: פנחס approaches שבט שמעון, leaning on his spear shaft, and pretends that he too wants to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: He walked along leaning on his staff. When he reached the tribe of שמעון, he said: Where do we find that the tribe of לוי is greater than the tribe of שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The story of פנחס continues. He reaches the men of שבט שמעון guarding the way and tells them that he is no better than they are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פנחס is using a trick. By saying לוי is no greater than שמעון, he hints that if they may sin with the Moabite women, so may he. This gets him past the guards without raising suspicion.

keyTerms.meaning: leaning
his staff (here, the shaft of his spear)
the tribe of שמעון, the tribe of זמרי
where do we find?

phrases.english: walking along, leaning on his staff,
phrases.notes: This picks up the story from before. The 'staff' is really the shaft of his spear.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן שֶׁהִגִּיעַ אֵצֶל שִׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל שִׁמְעוֹן
phrases.english: and once he reached the tribe of Shimon
he said: Where do we find

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁשִּׁבְטוֹ שֶׁל לֵוִי גָּדוֹל מִשֶּׁל שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: that the tribe of Levi is greater than that of Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of פנחס from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פנחס disguises his mission by claiming equality with שבט שמעון.

steps.title: שבט שמעון lets him in
steps.stepSummary: The men of שמעון let פנחס through, thinking he is coming to sin, and say that even the pious now allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Let him through, he too is going in to take care of his needs. The pious ones have permitted the thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The trick works. שבט שמעון lets פנחס pass, sure that he is going in to sin just like them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They misread פנחס completely. They even take his behavior as a sign that the religious people now approve of the sin, which shows how sure they felt in their sin.

keyTerms.meaning: leave him alone / let him through
his needs (a polite way to say intimacy)
the pious, those who hold themselves apart from sin

phrases.english: They said: Let him through,
he too is going in to take care of his needs.
phrases.notes: A polite way of saying he is going in to sin with the women, just like them.

phrases.english: The pious ones have permitted the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reaction to the trick of פנחס in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבט שמעון lets פנחס in, wrongly thinking the pious now allow the sin.

steps.title: Six miracles done for פנחס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן lists six miracles that allowed פנחס to kill זמרי and כזבי and get away safely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Six miracles were done for פנחס. One, זמרי should have pulled away and did not. One, he should have called out and did not. One, פנחס aimed exactly at the private parts of the man and of the woman. One, they did not slip off the spear. One, an angel came and raised the doorway's top beam. One, an angel came and caused destruction among the people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a numbered list of six miracles that helped פנחס do his act of zealotry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each miracle covers a different danger. The first two show that זמרי did nothing to stop it, the middle two show the killing was clear and visible, and the last two let פנחס leave safely. The point is that שמים was helping פנחס all the way.

keyTerms.meaning: miracles
to separate / pull away
he aimed precisely
spear
lintel, the top beam of a doorway
and caused destruction

steps.whyThisMatters: The list shows that the act of פנחס, though done on his own, had clear backing from שמים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Six miracles were done for Pinchas.
One, that Zimri should have pulled away
and he did not pull away.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד, שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ לְדַבֵּר וְלֹא דִּבֵּר.
phrases.english: And one, that he should have spoken out, and he did not speak.
phrases.notes: He means זמרי could have called his tribe for help, but he didn't.

phrases.english: And one, that he aimed exactly at the male organ of the man
and at the female organ of the woman.
And one, that they did not slip off the spear.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד, שֶׁבָּא מַלְאָךְ וְהִגְבִּיהַּ אֶת הַמַּשְׁקוֹף.
phrases.english: And one, that an angel came and raised the lintel.
And one, that an angel came and caused destruction among the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שִׁשָּׁה נִסִּים נַעֲשׂוּ לוֹ לְפִנְחָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After פנחס gets inside, רבי יוחנן describes the miracles that made the killing succeed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six miracles were done for פנחס when he killed זמרי and כזבי.

steps.title: פנחס protests before הקב"ה
steps.stepSummary: פנחס throws the bodies down before הקב"ה and asks whether 24,000 Jews should die because of these sinners.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and threw them down before הקב"ה and said: Master of the world, should 24,000 Jews fall because of these people? As it says: 'Those who died in the plague were 24,000.'
steps.whatsHappening: פנחס brings the two dead sinners before הקב"ה and protests the plague killing so many Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פנחס argues that the sinners have now been punished, so the many others should not die because of them. The פסוק from במדבר gives the number 24,000 that פנחס mentions.

keyTerms.meaning: and he threw them down hard
הקב"ה (literally, 'the Place')
Master of the world
plague

phrases.english: He came and threw them down before the Omnipresent,
he said before Him: Master of the world,
because of these shall fall
twenty-four thousand of Israel?
As it says: "And those who died in the plague were
twenty-four thousand."
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the killing, the story moves to what פנחס did next.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פנחס protested that 24,000 Jews should not die because of these sinners.

steps.title: The פסוק in תהלים describes this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the protest of פנחס is what the פסוק 'ויעמד פינחס ויפלל' is describing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And פנחס stood and judged.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the story to a פסוק in תהלים. This also sets up רבי אלעזר's reading of the word ויפלל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story of פנחס arguing with הקב"ה explains why the פסוק says he 'stood' and did something with words. The word ויפלל is unusual, and the next step will explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written
and he judged / pleaded a case

phrases.english: And that is what is written:
"And Pinchas stood and judged."
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:30

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the protest of פנחס in step 4 to a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The protest of פנחס before הקב"ה

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: פנחס argued a case with his Creator
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that the פסוק says ויפלל, not ויתפלל, showing that פנחס argued with הקב"ה like in a court case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It does not say 'and he prayed' but 'ויפלל.' This teaches that, so to speak, he argued a legal case with his Creator.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר explains the unusual word in the פסוק from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ויתפלל would mean a normal prayer. ויפלל comes from פלילות, judgment, so פנחס was not just asking. He was making a bold, legal-style argument against הקב"ה, which is why the text adds כביכול.

keyTerms.meaning: and he prayed
so to speak (used when speaking boldly about הקב"ה)
a judgment, a legal case
his Creator

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read ויפלל as plain prayer. רבי אלעזר's whole point is that it means arguing a case, not asking politely.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
It does not say "and he prayed" but rather "and he judged."
This teaches that, so to speak,
he argued a case with his Creator.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word ויפלל from the פסוק quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ויפלל teaches that פנחס argued a case with הקב"ה, not just prayed.

steps.title: הקב"ה defends פנחס against the angels
steps.stepSummary: The angels want to push פנחס away for speaking so boldly, but הקב"ה says to leave him, since he is a zealot from zealots and one who turns away anger from those who did the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ministering angels wanted to push him away. He said to them: Leave him alone. He is a zealot son of a zealot; he turns back anger, son of one who turned back anger.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with הקב"ה protecting פנחס from the angels who were upset at his bold words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels think פנחס went too far by arguing with הקב"ה. הקב"ה answers that this boldness runs in his family: zealotry from לוי, and stopping divine anger from אהרן. So his bold words are approved, not punished.

keyTerms.meaning: the ministering angels
to push him away
a zealot
one who turns back anger

steps.whatToRemember: פנחס acted as a zealot, was helped by six miracles, and then boldly argued with הקב"ה to stop the plague. הקב"ה backed him up because zeal and turning back anger run in his family.

phrases.english: The ministering angels wanted to push him away.
He said to them: Leave him alone,
he is a zealot, son of a zealot,
phrases.notes: He comes from לוי, who acted with zeal over what was done to דינה.

phrases.aramaic: מֵשִׁיב חֵימָה בֶּן מֵשִׁיב חֵימָה הוּא.
phrases.english: he is one who turns back anger, son of one who turned back anger.
phrases.notes: He descends from אהרן, who stopped the plague after the story of קרח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי אלעזר's teaching: after פנחס argues with הקב"ה, the angels object and הקב"ה defends him.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The bold argument of פנחס was accepted by הקב"ה because he follows in the ways of his zealous, peace-making ancestors.

steps.title: The tribes mock פנחס
steps.stepSummary: The שבטים insult פנחס for coming from a grandfather who fattened calves for idol worship, and yet daring to kill a נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The tribes began to put him down: 'Did you see this בן פוטי, whose mother's father fattened calves for עבודה זרה, and he killed a נשיא of a tribe of ישראל?'
steps.whatsHappening: The שבטים attack פנחס's right to act. They say someone from his background had no business killing a tribal leader.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their complaint mixes two points: his family background is shameful, and the person he killed was important. This sets up the next line, where the תורה answers them.

keyTerms.meaning: insulting, putting down
'son of Puti', a mocking nickname for פנחס
fattened (animals)
the prince or leader of a tribe

phrases.english: The tribes began to demean him:
Did you see this son of Puti,
phrases.notes: A mocking nickname. It plays on the word פיטם, 'fattened', in the next line.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁפִּיטֵּם אֲבִי אִמּוֹ עֲגָלִים לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: whose mother's father fattened calves for idol worship,
and he killed a prince of a tribe of Israel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After הקב"ה defends פנחס to the angels, the people now challenge him too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The legitimacy of פנחס's act of killing זמרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone descended from an idol worshipper cannot rightly kill a tribal leader.

steps.title: The פסוק traces his lineage to אהרן
steps.stepSummary: The תורה answers the mockers by listing פנחס's lineage back to אהרן הכהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק came and listed his lineage: 'פנחס בן אלעזר בן אהרן הכהן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the פסוק names his ancestors on purpose, to answer the insult from the שבטים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mockers pointed to his mother's side. The פסוק points to his father's side, which goes back to אהרן הכהן. This is the reason the פסוק lists his ancestors at all.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse came (to teach something)
traced his family line

phrases.english: The verse came and traced his lineage:
"Pinchas son of Elazar son of Aaron the priest."
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the mockery from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading of a פסוק: the lineage is listed to defend פנחס
steps.terutzHavaAmina: פנחס's background made his act improper.
steps.terutzMaskana: His father's line goes back to אהרן הכהן, so his act was fitting.

steps.title: הקב"ה tells משה to greet פנחס with peace
steps.stepSummary: הקב"ה tells משה to be the first to greet פנחס with peace. The atonement פנחס brought is fit to last forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to משה: 'Be the first to greet him with peace,' as it says: 'Therefore say: I am giving him My covenant of peace.' And this atonement is worthy of continuing to atone forever.
steps.whatsHappening: הקב"ה publicly honors פנחס through משה. The גמרא adds that his atonement for the people keeps working forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the insults, הקב"ה shows everyone that פנחס acted rightly. The 'covenant of peace' is read as משה greeting him first, and his atonement is described as lasting for all time.

keyTerms.meaning: be the first to greet him with peace
My covenant of peace
atonement

steps.whatToRemember: פנחס was mocked by people, but defended by the תורה and honored by הקב"ה, with a lasting atonement.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moshe:
Be the first to greet him with peace,
as it is said: "Therefore say:

phrases.aramaic: הִנְנִי נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶת בְּרִיתִי שָׁלוֹם״.
phrases.english: I am giving him My covenant of peace."
phrases.notes: במדבר 25:12

phrases.english: And this atonement is worthy
of continuing to atone forever.
phrases.notes: This connects to the next פסוק, במדבר 25:13, which talks about how he atoned for the people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending פנחס's lineage, the story moves on to his reward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקב"ה had משה greet פנחס with peace, and his atonement lasts forever.

steps.title: רב reads זרזיר as 424 and explains why פנחס waited
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רב explains a פסוק in משלי. זמרי sinned 424 times that day, and פנחס waited for him to weaken, not knowing that הקב"ה was with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: What does the פסוק 'The girded greyhound, or the he-goat, and a king with whom none can rise' mean? That wicked man had 424 acts of relations that day, and פנחס waited until his strength weakened. But פנחס did not know that 'the king with whom none can rise', הקב"ה, was with him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement explains a פסוק in משלי as hinting to this story. It tells us why פנחס waited before he struck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זרזיר adds up to 424, the number of times זמרי sinned. פנחס waited until זמרי was weak. But the end of the פסוק teaches that this was not needed, because הקב"ה was helping פנחס all along.

keyTerms.meaning: what is meant by what is written
a strong animal in the פסוק, here hinting to the number 424
a king with whom none can rise up (here: הקב"ה)
his strength weakened

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rav:
What is meant by what is written:
"The girded-loins greyhound, or the he-goat,
phrases.notes: משלי 30:31

phrases.english: and a king with whom none can rise up"?
Four hundred and twenty-four acts of relations
phrases.notes: That's the number value of זרזיר: 7+200+7+10+200 = 424.

phrases.english: that wicked one had on that day,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִמְתִּין לוֹ פִּנְחָס עַד שֶׁתָּשַׁשׁ כֹּחוֹ.
phrases.english: and Pinchas waited for him until his strength weakened.
But he did not know
that "a king with whom none can rise up" was with him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is פנחס, and the King is הקב"ה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new statement about the same story, explaining a פסוק from משלי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זמרי sinned 424 times (זרזיר), and פנחס waited, not knowing הקב"ה was with him.

steps.title: A ברייתא says sixty times
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives a different number, sixty, and describes how drained זמרי and כזבי were.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: sixty times, until he became like a spoiled egg, and she was like a garden bed full of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different count than רב's 424.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number goes from 424 down to sixty, but the point is the same: זמרי was completely drained. The pictures of a spoiled egg and a soaked garden bed show how worn out and disgraced they both were.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
a spoiled (addled) egg
a garden bed

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraisa: sixty,
until he became like an addled egg,
phrases.notes: An egg whose insides have turned to mush. He was totally drained.

phrases.english: and she was like a garden bed full of water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different number than רב's 424.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sixty times, until זמרי was completely drained.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב יוסף add details about כזבי
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב יוסף add exaggerated descriptions that show the disgrace of כזבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: And her seat was the size of a בית סאה. רב יוסף taught: Her womb was an אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more אמוראים add details about כזבי, continuing the ברייתא's description of her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are purposely exaggerated descriptions. Like the ברייתא, they stress how shameful the sin was.

keyTerms.meaning: a field area big enough to plant a סאה of seed
taught (a teaching passed down)
a cubit (an amah)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא describes זמרי and כזבי in extreme terms to show how great פנחס's act was, and that הקב"ה was with him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: וּמוֹשָׁבָהּ בֵּית סְאָה.
phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: And her seat was a beis se'ah.
phrases.notes: A beis se'ah is a field big enough to plant a סאה of seed.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב יוֹסֵף: קֶבֶר שֶׁלָּהּ אַמָּה.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef taught: Her womb was a cubit.
phrases.notes: קבר literally means 'grave'. Here it's used as a word for the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: וּמוֹשָׁבָהּ בֵּית סְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the ברייתא's description of כזבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exaggerated descriptions of כזבי that stress her disgrace.

steps.title: כזבי's real name and why she was called כזבי
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says כזבי's real name was שוילנאי בת צור. He gives two explanations for the nickname כזבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת says: Her name was not כזבי. Her name was שוילנאי בת צור. So why was she called כזבי? Because she went against what her father told her. Another explanation: she was called כזבי because she told her father, 'Slaughter this people through me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tells us that כזבי was a nickname, and her real name was שוילנאי בת צור. He then explains where the nickname came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations are word plays on the name כזבי. The first connects it to כזב, a lie or betrayal of her father. The second splits it into כוס בי, "slaughter through me," showing she wanted to bring ruin on בני ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The Midianite woman in the story with זמרי (במדבר 25:15)
Her real name, according to רב ששת
She lied, or went against (from the root כזב)
Another explanation
Slaughter

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet says:
Cozbi was not her name,
rather, Shevilnai daughter of Tzur was her name.
And why was she called Cozbi?
Because she went against her father.
phrases.notes: כִּזְּבָה sounds like כָּזְבִּי.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
Cozbi, because she said to her father:
"Slaughter this people through me."
phrases.notes: Put together, כּוֹס + בִּי sound like כָּזְבִּי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of כזבי's disgrace from step 13 by explaining her name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כזבי's real name was שוילנאי בת צור; כזבי is a nickname that hints at her betrayal or her wish to destroy בני ישראל.

steps.title: Folk sayings that use the name שוילנאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the name שוילנאי by quoting common sayings about a loose woman named שוילנאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what people say: 'Between the reeds and the willows, what is שוילנאי looking for?' And: 'Among the peels of the reeds, what is שוילנאי looking for?' She made her mother into a prostitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the name שוילנאי was known among people, because their sayings use it for a woman who goes looking for sin. This backs up רב ששת's claim about her real name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiding among reeds and willows hints at looking for a private place to sin. Her name became a byword for a loose woman, so her shame reached her mother too.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what people say
Reeds
Willows
She made her mother a prostitute (shamed her mother)

phrases.english: And this is what people say:
"Between reeds and willows,
what is Shevilnai looking for?"
"Among the peels of the reeds,
what is Shevilnai looking for?"
She made her mother into a prostitute.
phrases.notes: Her name became a word for a loose woman, so it shamed her mother too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רב ששת's claim from step 14 that her real name was שוילנאי.
steps.raayaObject: That כזבי's real name was שוילנאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Popular sayings that use the name שוילנאי for a woman looking for sin.

steps.title: The five names of זמרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן lists five names of זמרי and explains four of them as hints to his sin. His real name was שלומיאל בן צורישדי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: He has five names: זמרי, בן סלוא, שאול, בן הכנענית, and שלומיאל בן צורישדי. זמרי, because he became like a spoiled egg. בן סלוא, because he brought up the sins of his family. שאול, because he lent himself to sin. בן הכנענית, because he acted like the people of כנען. And what is his real name? שלומיאל בן צורישדי.
steps.whatsHappening: Just as כזבי had a nickname, רבי יוחנן says זמרי had several names. Each of the first four is read as a hint to his sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name gets a word play: זמרי with מוזרת (a spoiled egg), סלוא with הסליא (brought up sins), שאול with השאיל (lent himself). In the end רבי יוחנן says זמרי was really שלומיאל בן צורישדי, the נשיא of שבט שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: A spoiled egg that will not hatch
Brought up, stirred up
Lent
The deeds of Canaan (immoral behavior)
The נשיא of שבט שמעון; זמרי's real name

steps.whatToRemember: Both sinners in the story have "real" names behind their known names: כזבי was שוילנאי, and זמרי was שלומיאל בן צורישדי. Their known names are read as hints to their sin.
steps.confusionAlert: שאול here is not שאול המלך. It is one of the names given to זמרי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
He has five names:
phrases.notes: "He" means זמרי.

phrases.english: Zimri, and son of Salu, and Shaul,
and son of the Canaanite woman,
and Shelumiel son of Tzurishaddai.
Zimri, because he became like a spoiled egg,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן סָלוּא – עַל שֶׁהִסְלִיא עֲוֹנוֹת שֶׁל מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ,
phrases.english: son of Salu, because he brought up the sins of his family,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאוּל – עַל שֶׁהִשְׁאִיל עַצְמוֹ לִדְבַר עֲבֵירָה,
phrases.english: Shaul, because he lent himself to a sinful act,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן הַכְּנַעֲנִית – עַל שֶׁעָשָׂה מַעֲשֵׂה כְנַעַן,
phrases.english: son of the Canaanite woman, because he did the deeds of Canaan,
And what is his real name?
Shelumiel son of Tzurishaddai is his name.
phrases.notes: במדבר 1:6

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חֲמִשָּׁה שֵׁמוֹת יֵשׁ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 14: after the names of כזבי, the גמרא gives the names of זמרי, closing the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זמרי had five names; four hint at his sin, and his real name was שלומיאל בן צורישדי.

steps.title: Is a כהן who served while טמא liable to מיתה בידי שמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's case of a כהן who served while טמא. רב אחא בר הונא asks רב ששת if such a כהן is liable to מיתה בידי שמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A כהן who served while טמא. רב אחא בר הונא asked רב ששת: A כהן who served while טמא, is he liable to death at the hands of Heaven, or is he not liable to death at the hands of Heaven?
steps.whatsHappening: The story is over, and the גמרא returns to the next case in the משנה: a כהן who did the עבודה while טמא. This step sets up a new question, which will be answered in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says young כהנים may kill such a כהן on the spot, but it does not say what his punishment is from Heaven. רב אחא בר הונא wants to know if he is also liable to מיתה בידי שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן who did the עבודה in the מקדש while טמא
He asked him (a real question, not an attack)
Death at the hands of Heaven (not carried out by a בית דין)

steps.whyThisMatters: This starts a new legal discussion: the punishment for a כהן doing the עבודה while טמא.

phrases.english: "A kohen who served while impure."

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Huna asked Rav Sheshet:
A kohen who served while impure,
is he liable to death at the hands of Heaven

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵין חַיָּיב מִיתָה בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם?
phrases.english: or is he not liable to death at the hands of Heaven?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אַחָא בַּר הוּנָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the זמרי story and opens a new legal topic from the next case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כהן who did the עבודה while טמא is liable to מיתה בידי שמים.

steps.title: רב ששת proves from the משנה that the כהן is not liable
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the answer is in the משנה. The young כהנים kill the כהן, so he must not be liable to death by Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it. A כהן who served while טמא is not brought to court by his fellow כהנים. Instead, the young כהנים take him out of the עזרה and split his skull with pieces of wood. If he were liable to death by Heaven, they should just leave him and let Heaven kill him. So what must we say? He is not liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question from Step 17 with a proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says people kill this כהן right away. רב ששת reasons that if Heaven were already going to kill him, there would be no need for people to do it. So the משנה shows he has no מיתה בידי שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: You (already) learned it
Young כהנים, literally 'flowers of the כהונה'
The Temple courtyard
Pieces or sticks of wood
Death at the hands of Heaven

phrases.english: He said to him: You already learned it:
phrases.notes: רב ששת is answering רב אחא בר הונא's question from Step 17.

phrases.english: A כהן who served while טמא

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אֶחָיו הַכֹּהֲנִים מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין,
phrases.english: his brother כהנים do not bring him to court;
rather, the young כהנים
take him out of the עזרה
and split his skull with pieces of wood.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ מְחַיֵּיב בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: And if you think he is liable to death by Heaven,
let them leave him alone, so he will be killed by Heaven!
Rather, what must we say? He is not liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of Step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a כהן who served while טמא liable to מיתה בידי שמים?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The משנה has people kill him, which would make no sense if Heaven were going to kill him anyway.

steps.title: Can people kill someone the Torah exempts?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא rejects the proof. It makes no sense for people to kill someone the Torah lets go free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there anything for which the Torah exempts a person from death, and yet we get up and kill him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא attacks רב ששת's proof by turning it around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת said the כהן is not liable to death by Heaven. רב אחא בר הונא says the opposite logic is stronger. If the Torah gives him no death penalty at all, how could people be allowed to kill him? So the fact that he is killed suggests he IS liable to death by Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Exempted him

phrases.english: Is there anything
for which the Torah exempts him,
and we will get up and kill him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reasoning of רב ששת's proof from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: People cannot kill someone the Torah exempts from death, so the killing shows he must be liable.

steps.title: The case of one flogged who sinned again
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת shows a case where people do kill someone the Torah exempts: one who got lashes and repeated the sin is put into the כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is that not so? But we learned in a משנה: one who received lashes and then repeated the sin is put by the court into the כיפה. The Torah exempts him from death, and yet we kill him!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת challenges רב אחא בר הונא's rule with a case from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Getting lashes means the sin carries no death penalty. Yet the משנה says the court puts a repeat sinner into the כיפה, where he dies. So people do sometimes kill someone the Torah exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: Received lashes and repeated the sin
A narrow vaulted cell where the sinner is held until he dies

phrases.english: And is that not so? But we learned in a משנה:
One who received lashes and repeated the sin,
the court puts him into the כיפה.
The Torah exempts him, and we kill him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule stated in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר הונא's rule that people never kill someone the Torah exempts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A repeat sinner who only deserved lashes is put into the כיפה and dies.

steps.title: That case deals with sins punished by כרת
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא answers that the כיפה case is about lashes for sins that carry כרת, so the person already deserves death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי ירמיה say in the name of ריש לקיש: we are dealing with lashes for sins that carry כרת, where the man already deserves death?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא answers רב ששת's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some sins carry both lashes and כרת, which is a death from Heaven. The כיפה is only for those sins. So that person is not truly exempt from death, and the rule from Step 19 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven
A person who deserves death
We are dealing with

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: But didn't רבי ירמיה say in the name of ריש לקיש:
We are dealing with lashes for sins that carry כרת,
where the man already deserves death.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כיפה is for any repeat sinner who got lashes, even one not liable to death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כיפה is only for sins with כרת, so the sinner already deserves death from Heaven.

steps.title: The case of one who steals the קסוה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a second case: one who steals the קסוה is struck by zealots, even though the Torah gives no death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about one who steals the קסוה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tries another challenge to רב אחא בר הונא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says zealots may strike one who steals the קסוה. Stealing usually carries no death penalty in the Torah, so this looks like people killing someone the Torah exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: A kind of vessel, a jug or cup
One who steals

phrases.english: But what about one who steals the קסוה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 21 answered the first challenge, this brings a new one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that people never kill someone the Torah exempts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Zealots strike the thief of the קסוה, though stealing carries no death penalty.

steps.title: The קסוה is a כלי שרת, hinted to in a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא answers that the קסוה is a כלי שרת, and a פסוק hints that someone who takes holy vessels deserves death.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say: we are dealing with a כלי שרת, and it is hinted in the פסוק: 'They shall not come to see the holy things being covered, lest they die.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא answers the קסוה challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קסוה here is a holy vessel of the בית המקדש. The פסוק says one who improperly handles holy things will die. So this thief is connected to a death penalty, and he is not fully exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel used for the service in the בית המקדש
It is hinted
As it is being covered (or swallowed up)

phrases.english: But didn't רב יהודה say:
We are dealing with a כלי שרת,
and it is hinted in the פסוק:
'They shall not come to see
the holy things being covered, lest they die.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 4:20

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בִּכְלִי שָׁרֵת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) plus a hint from a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Stealing the קסוה is a plain theft with no death penalty at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a holy vessel, and a פסוק hints at death for this, so the thief is not truly exempt.

steps.title: The case of one who curses with the sorcerer
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a third case from the משנה: one who curses with the קוסם, whom zealots may strike.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about one who curses with the קוסם?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת tries a third challenge to רב אחא בר הונא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets zealots strike this person too. It looks like a curse that carries no death penalty in the Torah, so it seems people may kill someone the Torah exempts.

keyTerms.meaning: One who curses
Sorcerer or magician

phrases.english: But what about one who curses with the קוסם?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 23 answered the second challenge, this brings a third.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that people never kill someone the Torah exempts.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Zealots strike one who curses with the קוסם, though this curse seems to carry no death penalty.

steps.title: That curse is really aimed at ה׳'s Name
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא answers with רב יוסף's teaching. The curse is worded so that it looks like cursing ה׳'s Name, which is a serious sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יוסף teach: the case is where he says, 'Let the קוסם strike his קוסם,' which looks like 'blessing' the Name, meaning cursing ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא answers the third challenge, so each of רב ששת's cases has now been explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse is not really aimed at a simple magician. It is a hidden way of cursing ה׳. That links it to the serious sin of cursing the Name, so this person is not truly exempt either.

keyTerms.meaning: His sorcerer (here hinting at the one he worships)
'Blessing' the Name, a polite way of saying cursing ה׳

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת brought three cases where people seem to kill someone the Torah exempts: the כיפה, the קסוה, and the קוסם. Each time רב אחא בר הונא showed that the person is really connected to a death penalty.
steps.confusionAlert: 'מברך את השם' does not mean real blessing here. It is a polite way of saying cursing ה׳, so the words do not have to be said out loud.

phrases.english: But didn't רב יוסף teach:
'Let the קוסם strike his קוסם,'
which looks like 'blessing' the Name.
phrases.notes: 'Blessing' is a polite way to say cursing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He cursed an ordinary magician, which carries no death penalty.
steps.terutzMaskana: The curse is a hidden curse of ה׳'s Name, so the person is connected to a death penalty.

steps.title: The fourth case: one who lives with a non-Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת points to the משנה's case of בועל ארמית. The Torah gives this person no death penalty, yet קנאין may strike him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about one who lives with a non-Jewish woman? The Torah gives him no death penalty, and still zealots may strike him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings one more case to show that קנאין may strike someone who does not deserve death. This is the fourth case in the series.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר הונא answered each earlier case by showing that the sinner really did deserve death in some way. Here רב ששת picks the case the משנה is best known for, בועל ארמית. It looks like a sin with no Torah death penalty at all, so it seems to prove his point.

keyTerms.meaning: One who lives with a non-Jewish woman. The משנה says קנאין may strike him.
Zealots, people who act out of burning loyalty to ה׳.

phrases.english: But what about one who lives with an Aramean (non-Jewish) woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אחא בר הונא answered the קוסם case, רב ששת brings a new case in the same series.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר הונא's rule that people never kill someone the Torah exempts from death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בועל ארמית has no Torah death penalty, but the משנה still lets קנאין strike him. So striking does not require a death penalty.

steps.title: A dream and רב's tradition show this sin carries כרת
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא answers that a פסוק was read to רב כהנא in a dream, and רב then remembered his own tradition. Together these show that בועל ארמית is punished with כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wasn't a פסוק read to רב כהנא in his dream? And then רב remembered what he had learned as a tradition: such a person is cut off (כרת).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר הונא answers the fourth case. He shows that this sinner also deserves death, because the sin carries כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer points back to an earlier story. A פסוק was shown to רב כהנא in a dream, and it reminded רב of a tradition he had learned. That tradition teaches that ה׳ cuts off a man who lives with a non-Jewish woman. Since כרת is a death penalty from Heaven, this case also fits רב אחא בר הונא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They read to him, meaning someone recited a פסוק to him.
In his dream.
His learning, meaning a tradition he had received from his teachers.
Being cut off. A death penalty that comes from Heaven, not from a human court.

steps.whatToRemember: In all four cases (כיפה, קסוה, קוסם, ארמית), רב אחא בר הונא shows that the sinner already deserves death. So he keeps his rule that people never kill someone the Torah exempts from death.

phrases.english: Didn't they read a verse to רב כהנא in his dream,
and רב remembered his tradition?
phrases.notes: The tradition he remembered is that a man who does this is punished with כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ששת's fourth case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the case does carry a death penalty from Heaven (כרת), so it fits the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בועל ארמית has no death penalty, so קנאין strike even people who do not deserve death.
steps.terutzMaskana: בועל ארמית is liable to כרת, so he also already deserves death.

steps.title: A ברייתא about Temple tasks done outside the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא now challenges רב ששת with a ברייתא. It lists Temple tasks that, if done outside the מקדש, carry no punishment. It then starts listing other ways one is not liable for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him from a ברייתא: A כהן who pours oil, mixes it in, breaks the מנחה into pieces, salts it, waves it, brings it near the מזבח, arranges the שולחן, cleans out the lamps, takes the קמיצה, or collects the blood, if he does any of these outside the מקדש, he is exempt. And one is not liable for them...
steps.whatsHappening: Now the roles flip. רב אחא בר הונא challenges רב ששת's view that a כהן who serves while טמא does not deserve death. This step is the opening of the ברייתא, which continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists smaller Temple tasks and says that doing them outside the מקדש brings no punishment. The words 'and one is not liable for them' start a second list of exemptions for these same tasks. The challenge to רב ששת will become clear once the ברייתא finishes this list.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him. Used when someone attacks a view by quoting a משנה or ברייתא.
The one who takes the קמיצה, a fistful of flour taken from a מנחה.
The one who arranges the שולחן, setting out the לחם הפנים.
The one who cleans and prepares the lamps of the מנורה.
Outside the מקדש.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ברייתא is finished here. 'And one is not liable for them' is the start of a new sentence that continues right after this. The challenge to רב ששת depends on the rest of it.

phrases.english: He challenged him: One who pours oil, and one who mixes it in, and one who breaks a meal-offering into pieces,
phrases.notes: Now it is רב אחא בר הונא challenging רב ששת, the opposite of the earlier steps.

phrases.english: one who salts, one who waves, one who brings it near the altar,
and one who arranges the Table,
one who cleans out the lamps,
and one who takes the handful, and one who collects the blood
